## Introduction

Do all penguin species have a similar body mass? In this post, I use
Python to compare the average body mass of Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo
penguins. I first check the data, remove records with missing body mass,
and then summarize and plot the results.

## Data source

I use the [Palmer Penguins dataset](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.
The data is available under a CC0 licence.

Dataset package citation: Horst, Hill, and Gorman (2020),
[palmerpenguins](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3960218).

The Python package includes the data, so this post does not need to
download a separate CSV when it runs.

## Set up

```{python}
#| label: python-setup

import sys
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

print(sys.executable)
```

## Explore the data

I load the dataset and check its size and first few rows.

```{python}
#| label: explore-penguins

penguins = load_penguins()

print("Number of rows:", penguins.shape[0])
print("Number of columns:", penguins.shape[1])

penguins.head()
```

The dataset contains 344 penguins. For this analysis, I focus on the
species and body mass columns. Body mass is measured in grams.

## Check missing values

Before calculating averages, I check whether any body mass values
are missing.

```{python}
#| label: clean-penguins

print(penguins[["species", "body_mass_g"]].isna().sum())

penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["species", "body_mass_g"])

print("Rows remaining:", len(penguins_clean))
print("Rows removed:", len(penguins) - len(penguins_clean))
```

Two penguins have missing body mass values, leaving 342 records for
the comparison. I only remove rows missing values needed for this
analysis. Missing values in other columns do not affect this comparison.

## Average body mass by species

I group the remaining records by species and calculate the number of
penguins and their average body mass.

```{python}
#| label: summarize-penguins

species_summary = (
    penguins_clean
    .groupby("species", as_index=False)
    .agg(
        count=("body_mass_g", "size"),
        mean_body_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "mean")
    )
    .sort_values("mean_body_mass_g")
)

species_summary.round(1)
```

Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass, at approximately
5,076 grams. Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have similar averages,
at approximately 3,701 and 3,733 grams.

## Compare the averages visually

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-body-mass
#| fig-cap: "Average body mass by penguin species, excluding records with missing body mass."

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))

ax.bar(
    species_summary["species"],
    species_summary["mean_body_mass_g"],
    color=["#4477AA", "#228833", "#CCBB44"]
)

ax.set_xlabel("Penguin species")
ax.set_ylabel("Average body mass (g)")
ax.set_title("Average body mass by species")
ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Conclusion

In this dataset, Gentoo penguins have a higher average body mass than
the other two species. Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have much closer
averages.

This comparison only describes group averages. It does not show the
variation within each species or account for differences in the
proportion of male and female penguins. A useful next step would be
to compare body mass by both species and sex.
